text:
alex: FYI I opened https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/482 — TF module slimming + provider pin changes. Ran a plan in staging and saw a handful of replacements. Can someone sanity-check before I run the state moves?

maya: coming in — ping the plan output you saw?

alex: pasted the relevant bits below. TL;DR: we hoisted a few resources out of module.network -> module.network-lite, and we updated provider sources to the new registry layout which Terraform interprets as a replace unless we map providers. Plan snippet: 
```
-/+ module.network.aws_route_table.main (aws_route_table -> aws_route_table)
-/+ module.network.aws_subnet.public[2] (resource to be replaced)
+ module.network-lite.aws_route_table.main will be created
+ module.network-lite.aws_subnet.public[2] will be created
```
Also got this warning: 
```
Warning: Provider source changed
 The module now requires registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws (v4.35.0), previously used registry.terraform.io/terraform-aws-modules/aws
```
And I have new k8s secret names in the helm values: `redwood-db-creds` -> `redwood-db/credentials` (we moved to namespace-scoped secret naming). I want to be careful with secrets wiring in k8s provider and the state move.

samir: ok. Two things: first, provider source changes are the common gotcha — Terraform treats that as a different provider so resources are orphaned unless you run `terraform state replace-provider` or migrate state to the new provider mapping. If the source changed but ABI is compatible, use `terraform state replace-provider 'registry.terraform.io/terraform-aws-modules/aws' 'registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws'` in a preflight step.

jordan: and for the module split, make sure the resource addresses are stable. If you changed module paths, you'll need `terraform state mv` from `module.network.aws_subnet.public[2]` -> `module.network-lite.aws_subnet.public[2]`. Do not apply until those moves are done, otherwise you may destroy/create.

maya: question about lockfile: did `init` regenerate a `.terraform.lock.hcl` with the new provider? That can change provider checksums and cause `terraform plan` to show differences.

alex: yes, I re-ran `terraform init` after changing provider blocks and it wrote a new lockfile. Plan was run after that. I kept provider versions pinned in the module `required_providers` to `~> 4.35`.

samir: good. Order of ops I recommend: 1) run `terraform providers mirror` / CI to ensure lockfile is committed, 2) in staging workspace run `terraform state replace-provider` if source changed, 3) run `terraform state mv` for module address changes, 4) run `terraform plan` to confirm no changes, 5) apply. For a subset, you can use `-target` to be cautious.

alex: sounds right. For secrets wiring — the helm chart change updates values from `secrets.name` to `secrets.namespace/name`. The k8s provider in our TF uses `manifest` to create `kubernetes_secret` resources. If we rename, state mv will handle it, but we also need to update any references in other modules that use `kubernetes_secret.data`.

jordan: small gotcha: some modules reference the secret via `kubectl`/external data source and expect a specific name. I'd add a short migration script to create a compatibility secret (old name -> new name) for a week and then fold the references. Keeps apps running during rollout.

maya: can we add a CI gate that runs `terraform plan` in a dedicated migration job that checks for `-/+` (replace) counts and fails if > X? We had an incident last quarter where a replace wiped external state.

alex: yep I'll add a gate. Also can someone run `terraform state replace-provider` in staging with me? I don't want to accidentally run against production.

samir: I can pair after lunch. Quick checklist I'll follow: 
- backup state snapshot (upload to S3 snapshot bucket)
- run `terraform state replace-provider` in staging
- run `terraform state mv` for all module address changes (I can script it if you paste a mapping)
- verify `terraform plan` shows no diffs
- coordinate a small canary apply in staging and then prod window

deploy-bot: [automated] scheduled backup of tfstate for workspace "staging" completed (snapshot: s3://tfstate-backups/infra-staging-2141598765.tar.gz) :white_check_mark:

alex: nice, thanks deploy-bot. I'll paste the mapping for `state mv` in the PR comments and add the CI gate. For the provider replace step I'll add an `ops/manual` runbook section so we can approve it.

jordan: quick nit: when you script the `state mv`, include `-backup` flags or do a separate state copy so ops can recover easily.

maya: :thumbsup: Sounds like a plan. LMK when you want a pair to run the commands.

alex: planning to do staging tomorrow 09:30 PT, will @samir and @maya. Thanks everyone — will update the PR with mapping and runbook.
